key_insight: RGR builds stochastic gradient estimators in Euclidean space and then retracts them onto the Stiefel manifold, removing the need for vector transport and enabling adaptive, horizon-free optimization.
engineering_relevance: This makes large-scale constrained learning on orthogonality-aware models, such as PCA and orthogonal CNNs, more practical by reducing tuning burden and improving stability in nonconvex training.
method: Construct recursive gradient estimators in Euclidean space, then map them to the tangent space before retraction.
Provide three variants: RGR-SPIDER for finite-sum problems, and RGR-SRM / RGR-EMA for online stochastic optimization.
Use adaptive stepsizes that avoid prior knowledge of Lipschitz constants, iteration horizons, and restrictive large-batch requirements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity guarantees and empirical gains on PCA, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal convolutional neural networks versus tangent-space recursive baselines.
watch_item: Performance still depends on manifold-specific implementation details and the practical cost of retraction and estimator updates may vary across applications.
paper_title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
